applicable_conditions: When the scoring criteria reward destroying the carrier over other ships (as implied by the large damage pool).
When the surface group's defense is layered and needs to be overwhelmed by mass.
When total missile inventory is limited and must be prioritized.
counter_conditions: If the carrier's damage points exceed the cumulative damage of the entire attack force, focusing on it will not yield a kill and may leave other targets untouched.
If the enemy has multiple high-value ships worth nearly equal points, splitting the salvo may secure more total kills.
If the carrier's defensive systems are superior to escorts, a focused attack might be wasted.
hypothesis: Concentrating the majority of the missile inventory on a single primary target (such as a carrier) is more effective at achieving mission objective (target destruction) than spreading fire across multiple targets, but it may fail to secure kills if the target's damage threshold is too high.

details: Step 1: Surface ships fire 90% of YJ-18s at the carrier.
Step 2: J-15s launch a small attack on the most damaged escort (e.g., DDG with 99% damage) to secure a kill.
Step 3: If the carrier survives, accept the partial damage while still destroying other units.
recommended_pattern.summary: Focus all heavy surface-launched missiles on the carrier to degrade it significantly, but allocate at least two J-15s or a final follow-up salvo to finish off lightly damaged escorts that may need only a few hits.
